fields.ic_name: AMBA AXI / ACE Protocol Specification (ARM IHI 0022E)
typical_axi_read_sequence_inherited: 1. Master drives AR* fields including ARDOMAIN/ARSNOOP/ARBAR; asserts ARVALID.
2. Slave (or interconnect) asserts ARREADY; AR handshake completes.
3. Slave drives R channel beats with RID, RDATA, RRESP[3:0] (RRESP[3:2] = IsShared/PassDirty), RLAST.
4. Master asserts RREADY per beat; final beat RLAST=1.
5. Master pulses RACK one cycle after the final beat's handshake.
typical_axi_write_sequence_inherited: 1. Master drives AW* fields including AWDOMAIN/AWSNOOP/AWBAR; asserts AWVALID.
2. Master drives W beats with WDATA/WSTRB/WLAST; asserts WVALID.
3. AW and W handshakes complete (any order).
4. Slave drives BRESP[2:0] (with BRESP[2]=DataTransfer for pass-dirty cases) + BVALID.
5. Master pulses WACK one cycle after the B handshake.
ace_coherent_read_sequence_ReadShared: 1. Cache miss in master M0: line not present, want shareable copy.
3. Interconnect identifies other Inner-shareable masters and broadcasts snoops on AC.
4. Each snooped master: applies ACSNOOP=ReadShared, computes new line state per Table C5-4, returns CRRESP.
5. If any snooped cache had UD/SD line: returns PassDirty=1, DataTransfer=1, ships dirty data on CD.
6. Interconnect aggregates: chooses data source (snooped CD dirty, or memory fetch).
7. Interconnect returns R data with RRESP[3:2] = (IsShared OR'd across snoops, PassDirty if responsibility transferred).
8. M0 receives line; installs as SC / SD / UC / UD per RRESP[3:2].
9. M0 pulses RACK; interconnect releases snoop ordering hazard.
ace_coherent_read_sequence_ReadUnique: 1. M0 wants exclusive ownership (e.g., about to do a write).
3. Interconnect snoops all other coherent masters with ACSNOOP=ReadUnique.
4. Each snooped master: invalidates its line (-> I); if was Dirty, returns PassDirty=1, DataTransfer=1 with data on CD; IsShared MUST be 0.
5. Interconnect aggregates: at most one snooped master can have had dirty data; merges into response.
6. R returns line with RRESP[3]=0, RRESP[2]=PassDirty.
7. M0 installs as UC or UD; pulses RACK.
ace_make_unique_sequence_full_line_overw: 1. M0 plans to write a complete cache line — no need to read current value.
2. M0 issues MakeUnique (ARSNOOP=0b1100); single RDATA beat returned (RDATA value is ignored).
3. Interconnect snoops others with ACSNOOP=MakeUnique; targets invalidate without returning data.
4. R returns RLAST=1 single beat; M0 pulses RACK.
5. M0 then issues WriteBack (AWSNOOP=0b011) to commit the new line.
ace_clean_invalid_software_flush_sequenc: 1. Software issues a flush-and-invalidate of address X via DC CIVAC (or similar) -> hardware emits CleanInvalid.
3. Interconnect snoops all coherent masters with ACSNOOP=CleanInvalid.
4. Each snooped cache: if line was UD/SD, returns PassDirty=1 + DataTransfer=1 with dirty data on CD; line transitions to I.
5. Memory is updated with the dirty data via the interconnect.
6. R returns single beat (data ignored); M0 pulses RACK.
7. Line is invalid in all caches; subsequent reads will fetch from memory.
ace_writeback_eviction_sequence: 1. M0 cache must evict a UD or SD line (replacement victim).
2. M0 issues WriteBack (AWSNOOP=0b011, AWDOMAIN matching the line's shareability).
3. M0 sends dirty data on W channel; WLAST=1 on the final beat.
4. Interconnect routes WriteBack to memory; B response OKAY.
5. M0 pulses WACK; line is removed from M0's cache.
ace_dvm_tlb_invalidate_sequence: 1. CPU executes a TLBI VA instruction -> initiates a DVM message.
2. Hardware emits DVMMessage (ARSNOOP=0b1111) with the TLB-invalidate payload encoded in address fields.
3. Interconnect distributes the DVMMessage via AC to all DVM nodes in the named shareability domain.
4. Each DVM node invalidates the relevant TLB entry; responds on CR.
5. After all DVM responses collected, initiator emits DVMComplete (ARSNOOP=0b1110); interconnect aggregates and signals completion.
ace_barrier_sequence_synchronization: 1. Software executes DSB SY (or similar synchronization barrier).
2. Hardware emits Barrier on AR or AW with AxBAR=0b11 (Synchronization), AxSNOOP=0 (read) or 0 (write), AxDOMAIN selecting the barrier scope.
3. Interconnect must observe the barrier: no transactions on either side of the barrier may be reordered across the barrier within the named domain.
4. Barrier completion: B response (write barrier) or R response (read barrier) — single beat, data ignored.
ace_lite_coherent_write_sequence_WriteLi: 1. ACE-Lite master (e.g., DMA controller) wants to push a fresh full line into the coherency domain.
3. Interconnect snoops cached masters with ACSNOOP=MakeUnique-equivalent; they invalidate any local copy.
4. ACE-Lite master pushes W data; B response returned.
5. ACE-Lite master pulses WACK; line is exclusively present at memory (visible to subsequent coherent reads).

ordering_rules_summary_ace.snoop_ordering: Each snoop transaction is fully ordered: response on CR must follow the order of addresses on AC.
ordering_rules_summary_ace.RACK_WACK_gating: Interconnect must observe RACK/WACK before issuing dependent snoops.
ordering_rules_summary_ace.barriers: Barrier transactions enforce ordering across the named shareability domain (Memory or Synchronization).

evidence.quote: The ACE protocol provides hardware cache coherency support and is an extension of the AXI4 protocol.
ARSNOOP encodings define the coherent read transaction types: ReadOnce, ReadShared, ReadClean, ReadNotSharedDirty, ReadUnique, CleanUnique, MakeUnique, CleanShared, CleanInvalid, MakeInvalid, DVM.
A snoop response is required on the snoop response channel for each snoop address that is presented to a cached master on the snoop address channel.
Permitted end states for combinations of initial state and snoop transaction.
